title: Jupyter kernelspec rootfs contract

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: Jupyter identity starts before execution: kernelspec argv and resource paths decide which interpreter/kernel will actually start.
hypothesis: `jupyter_client.kernelspec.KernelSpecManager' should expose at least one Python kernelspec in production, and its absolute argv/resource paths should resolve inside the selected rootfs rather than through host state.
predicted_behavior: Production mode should contain a usable Python kernelspec whose argv points at the rootfs Python interpreter or a resolvable rootfs-owned command.
observed_behavior: prod=t python="/usr/bin/python3" jupyter="/usr/bin/jupyter" status=0 python-specs=((("name" . "python3") ("resource_dir" . "/usr/share/jupyter/kernels/python3") ("argv" "/usr/bin/python3" "-Xfrozen_modules=off" "-m" "ipykernel_launcher" "-f" "{connection_file}"))) selected-launcher="/usr/bin/python3" launcher-path="/usr/bin/python3" bad-paths=nil

independent_checks.name: kernelspec manager ran in production
kernelspec paths have no forbidden host prefixes

counterexample: A notebook can print the expected result while attached to a host kernelspec with a different Python, package set, CUDA stack, or filesystem view.
derived_gym_requirement: Jupyter benchmarks must grade kernelspec identity before kernel execution and reject host-resolved kernel launchers.
